:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
The row echelon form matrix $B$ is given below. What are its pivot columns?
![](images/ce/ce4c17b3e47f0618d315e8e61feeb2b58cd913e54b63a3a375b8bd4676efbc8e.svg)
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that the pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.

We can see that $B$ has $3$ pivots in the $2$nd, $3$rd, and $4$th columns:

![](images/31/31b76b7840d750cf7cf060c5d218644f8733d46a0b59c0e347aeb634ea6c1091.svg)

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
The row echelon form matrix $C$ is given below. What are its **non**-pivot columns?

![](images/b1/b1f927457c74f57ff2e7cdb9d030492fffcb49bdfd9199e8720d3da2263e0b1e.svg)
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that the pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.

We can see that $C$ has $3$ pivots in the $1$st, $3$rd, and $4$th columns:

![](images/05/05264585d59a4430f5424b91f649eecc80a5f28fa460a935f5c224882e08d56c.svg)

Therefore, the only non-pivot column is the $2$nd column.

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Finding the Non-Pivot Columns of a Matrix in Row Echelon Form

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Determine the number of pivot columns of the matrix $A,$ given by
![](images/df/dfe650778e528254fc2098714566d954c47442ede485d6a92495cf16eb9e936d.svg)
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
First, we need to convert $A$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & -6 & 1 & 4\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $A$ has $3$ pivots, and therefore the number of pivot columns is $3.$

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Finding the Number of Pivot Columns of a Matrix

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
What are the pivot columns of the matrix $B,$ given by
![](images/f1/f10a5ef881920312ccdb163d9db70779d3848f7dc510c29d516eaf74a5ddd38d.svg)
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
First, we need to convert $B$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}B & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+(-\frac{2}{7}){R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix} & \end{aligned}
$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $B$ has $3$ pivots. In particular, the pivot columns are the $1$st, $3$rd, and $4$th columns.
